title: How to Start a Business? Don’t Wait for Permission.
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast

stated_problem.quote: And so I started selling golf balls out of necessity because I just wanted some side money.
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: Yard golf ball sales
idea.one_liner: Sell recovered golf balls to golfers who pass the house.
idea.offer: Washed golf balls sold from the home
idea.revenue_model: Direct sales by the ball bundle

key_quotes.quote: I'd put them in a wagon and I got this big piece of plywood and some paint and I put golf balls, three for a dollar.

claims.claim: Sold three golf balls for one dollar.
claims.quote: I'd put them in a wagon and I got this big piece of plywood and some paint and I put golf balls, three for a dollar.

claims.claim: Made hundreds of dollars, though he does not remember whether that was per summer, week, or month.
claims.quote: And I made hundreds of dollars a summer or a week or a month. I don't even remember.

acquisition_channels.details: A roadside mailbox sign drew golfers to the house to buy.

ideas.delivery: He collected and washed golf balls, then sold them from his home.

stated_problem.quote: People drop them and the screens break.
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: iPhone repair stores
idea.one_liner: Repair customers' broken iPhones at retail stores and charge per repair.
idea.revenue_model: Charge for each repair

key_quotes.quote: And people would come in with broken iPhones and I would say, "Okay, it's $80."

claims.claim: The business began in 2010, three years after the iPhone launched.
claims.quote: And then I learned about these guys in Louisiana that opened an iPhone repair store. And this was 2010. iPhone had come out three years before, but it was still brand new.

claims.claim: He asked an investor for $20,000 to start the store.
claims.quote: And I need $20,000. I want to start the store. I really think it's going to go well.

claims.claim: He quoted customers $80 for a repair.
claims.quote: And people would come in with broken iPhones and I would say, "Okay, it's $80."

claims.claim: He opened four stores over the next two years and sold them to a competitor.
claims.quote: So, I ended up opening four of those stores over the next two years and then sold them to a competitor.

acquisition_channels.details: Customers came into the stores with broken iPhones.
He says they did marketing but does not name the channels.

ideas.delivery: He repaired phones in retail stores, learning repairs on YouTube while working.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK consumer rights apply to repair services; protect any customer data accessible on devices under UK GDPR.

idea.name: LCD Cycle
idea.one_liner: Sell iPhone parts to repair shops and collect their broken screens for recycling in China.
idea.offer: Phone parts and a paid collection route for broken screens sent for remanufacturing
idea.revenue_model: Parts sales; the screen collection payment and resale economics are not fully described

key_quotes.quote: So, we started selling iPhone parts to repair shops and then getting their old broken screens recycled in China.

claims.claim: The company offered repair shops $3 for each broken iPhone screen.
claims.quote: And we would get our foot in the door with iPhone repair shops, the one like the one I just had, by saying, "Hey, we'll pay you $3 for every broken iPhone screen."

claims.claim: They ran the business for nine years.
claims.quote: That was we had that business for 9 years and it grew like a rocket ship, just super fast.

acquisition_channels.details: They approached iPhone repair shops with an offer to pay for their broken screens; the specific outreach method is not stated.

ideas.delivery: They sold parts to repair shops, collected broken screens, and shipped them to China for remanufacturing and recycling.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK waste shipment and recycling rules may apply to exporting broken screens; UK GDPR applies to any customer contact data.
